questions.q: What does your team already run well?
questions.hint: The post says switching has a real cost, so it counts.

options.label: MongoDB
options.why: your team already runs MongoDB well, and the post says switching has a real cost

options.label: Cassandra
options.why: your team already runs Cassandra well, and the post says switching has a real cost

questions.q: How well do you know your queries?

options.label: Not yet, and they keep changing
options.why: you can add an index as new questions arrive

options.label: I have a fixed list
options.why: Cassandra builds one table for each query

options.label: Lots of filters and aggregations
options.why: MongoDB has aggregation stages and $lookup, and Cassandra has no joins

questions.q: What does your write traffic look like?

options.label: Constant and huge, across several sites
options.why: any Cassandra replica can accept a write, with a consistency level you choose

options.label: Normal app traffic
options.why: normal traffic means nothing forces a move

questions.q: Do you need transactions across several documents or rows?

options.label: Only one-row conditional writes
options.why: Cassandra offers lightweight transactions for one-row conditions

options.label: No, each write stands alone
options.why: each write stands alone, which the post says suits Cassandra, and nothing forces a move

questions.q: Does the licence matter to you?

options.label: Yes, I want an Apache-licensed project
options.why: Cassandra uses the Apache License 2.0, and MongoDB's server uses the SSPL

options.label: No, either licence is fine
options.why: licence will not decide it for you

mongodb.name: MongoDB
mongodb.summary: A document database that stores flexible, JSON-like documents and is the easier one to query.
mongodb.bestWhen: you cannot list all your queries up front and your records are nested documents read whole.
mongodb.watchOut: documents top out at 16 MiB, an unindexed query on a big collection can be slow, and the server uses the SSPL licence, so read the terms.

cassandra.name: Cassandra
cassandra.summary: A masterless, Apache-2.0 database built for constant writes across many servers or sites.
cassandra.bestWhen: you know your queries, write all the time and want any replica to take a write.
cassandra.watchOut: no joins, one table per query, eventual consistency by default, and regular repair work for whoever runs it.

keep.name: Keep what you run
keep.summary: If your team already runs one of them well, the post says to stay with it.
keep.bestWhen: your team already runs one of the two well and nothing here forces a move.
keep.watchOut: staying put does not remove the limits the post lists, such as no joins on Cassandra or the 16 MiB document cap on MongoDB.
